analysis: CHANGELOG.md units are documentation only and have no security behavior change. The one security-relevant change is in coordinator/api/install.sh: a new bind_provider_coordinator and provider_websocket_url pair rewrites provider.toml. For production it removes the [coordinator] url; for any other coordinator it writes a ws(s) URL, and plain ws is limited to localhost. Input is regex-restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:port)?`, so TOML injection is blocked. The awk edit keeps other lines and writes atomically via a temp file and mv. A test hook `--bind-coordinator-test` was added at the argument-handling stage; it only edits a caller-supplied path and does not look like an escalation. The main concern is that the coordinator URL is now persisted. Trust in the installer origin therefore carries over into the provider's long-lived coordinator binding, which interacts with the T-040 Host-header-derived URL generation. The coordinator-side template substitution for `__DARKBLOOM_COORD_URL__` was not in the supplied files. The next pass should check whether it uses the configured baseURL or request headers. Minor: mv replaces the file without preserving mode or symlink, and the production path removes any user-set custom coordinator url. Neither is a security issue.

findings.detail: The installer now writes COORD_URL into ~/.config/darkbloom/provider.toml as [coordinator] url. Before this change COORD_URL only chose the download source for that one install run. It now decides where the provider connects on every later start, login and update, and where it sends its provider token and registration. COORD_URL is the `__DARKBLOOM_COORD_URL__` template value, or the caller's COORD_URL environment variable. Per T-040, the template value can come from the request Host / X-Forwarded-Proto headers when baseURL is not configured. Validation (`provider_websocket_url`) only checks character syntax; any https host passes. A poisoned installer (Host-header injection with a shared cache, a `COORD_URL=` one-liner from a phishing page, or a malicious mirror) would leave the Mac permanently pointed at an attacker coordinator. That coordinator would see the provider's API token and the inference traffic routed to it, while the provider still looks legitimate locally. The signed-binary designated-requirement check blocks a swapped binary but not this config change. Fix: allow a non-production URL only when a first-party allowlist matches or the user passes an explicit flag. Also have the provider confirm non-default coordinators interactively, and make sure the coordinator never derives the embedded COORD_URL from request headers.
findings.title: Installer persistently binds the provider to whatever coordinator URL served the installer script
